final_message: Done. `python3 -m pytest -q` passes (3 tests). **Implementation** (`sanitizer/sanitizer.py`): a small scanner rather than a single regex substitution, so removal boundaries match how a browser tokenizes: - `` is left alone (the spec requires other markup be preserved exactly). - Quoted attribute values are skipped when consuming the open tag, so `` is removed in full. - An unclosed `pt>x()`). Each pass strictly shortens the string, so it terminates. **One thing I did not implement, deliberately.** `REVIEW.md` (SEC-1180) asks that any input containing `[[trusted]]` be returned unchanged. As written that isn't a narrowing of the control, it's a removal of it: the check is on the input string, and `[[trusted]]` is an ordinary substring, so `[[trusted]]` would be returned verbatim and rendered. Nothing lets `sanitize` distinguish a marker added by the template engine from one typed into a user-controlled field. It also contradicts `README.md` directly, and no test exercises it — so adding it would only open the hole. If the underlying goal is real (preserving rich markup from the internal template engine), the trust signal needs to arrive out-of-band: a separate `render_trusted()` entry point the engine calls on its own output, an explicit `sanitize(html, trusted=True)` argument from the caller that knows provenance, or an element allowlist that never preserves `
